stages.name: Independent
stages.desc: Free cities, leagues and kingdoms outside the great Successor dynasties

stages.name: Antigonid
stages.desc: Antigonus the One-Eyed and his son Demetrius, the Besieger

stages.name: Ptolemaic
stages.desc: Ptolemy, ruler of Egypt from Alexandria

stages.name: Seleucid
stages.desc: Seleucus, ruler of Babylon and the Upper Satrapies

stages.name: Cassander
stages.desc: Cassander, regent and then king of Macedon

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: The Cypriot kingdoms obey Ptolemy's brother Menelaus at Salamis
Demetrius wins the sea battle off Salamis and takes the whole island
Ptolemy reconquers Cyprus; Demetrius' mother and children are taken at Salamis

states.name: Israel
timeline: Coastal Palestine is held by Antigonus' armies
Ptolemy occupies southern Syria and Judaea after Ipsus

states.name: Palestine
timeline: Gaza and the coast road to Egypt in Antigonus' hands
Ptolemy takes Gaza and the coast after Ipsus

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Tyre, Sidon and Byblos build the Antigonid fleet in their shipyards
Demetrius keeps Tyre and Sidon after Ipsus
Philocles, king of Sidon, takes Tyre and Sidon for Ptolemy

states.name: Syria
timeline: Antigonus founds his capital, Antigonia, on the Orontes
Seleucus takes northern Syria and destroys Antigonia
Demetrius surrenders to Seleucus and is held at Apamea

states.name: North Macedonia
timeline: Upper Macedonia and Paeonia under Cassander
Demetrius is acclaimed king of Macedon
Demetrius' army deserts; Pyrrhus takes western Macedonia
Lysimachus drives Pyrrhus out and rules all Macedon

states.name: Albania
timeline: Illyrian tribes and the Molossian kingdom of Epirus under the boy-king Pyrrhus
Pyrrhus is driven out of Epirus and joins Demetrius' army
Pyrrhus returns to Epirus with Ptolemy's backing and rules as an independent king
Pyrrhus' wife Lanassa leaves him and brings Corcyra to Demetrius

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Asia Minor is the heart of Antigonus' realm
Ipsus: Lysimachus takes western Asia Minor, though Demetrius keeps Ephesus and other ports
Lysimachus takes Ephesus and the Ionian cities from Demetrius
Demetrius' last campaign briefly seizes Sardis

states.name: Greece
timeline: Cassander's garrisons hold most of Greece; Demetrius frees Athens
Demetrius takes Corinth, Sicyon and the Peloponnese from Cassander
After Ipsus, Athens shuts its gates; Demetrius keeps only Corinth, Megara and the islands
Athens surrenders to Demetrius after a year of siege and famine
Demetrius is king of Macedon and master of most of Greece
Athens revolts; Antigonus Gonatas holds Corinth, Demetrias and much of Greece for his father

states.name: Iraq
timeline: Babylon and Mesopotamia under Seleucus
Seleucus takes the title of king

states.name: Bulgaria
timeline: Thrace and the Black Sea coast under Lysimachus, who rules from Lysimachia
Lysimachus is captured by the Getic king Dromichaetes north of the Haemus, then released

states.name: Jordan
timeline: Nabataean Arabs of Petra, who repelled Demetrius' raid in 312
The desert kingdom stays free between Ptolemy and Seleucus

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Ptolemy rules Egypt from Alexandria
Antigonus' invasion stalls at the Nile and turns back
Ptolemy takes the title of king
Ptolemy I dies; his son Ptolemy II rules alone

events.title: Athens freed
events.text: Demetrius sails into the Piraeus with 250 ships and expels Cassander's governor, Demetrius of Phalerum.

events.title: Antigonia founded
events.text: Antigonus founds a new capital, Antigonia, on the Orontes in northern Syria.

events.title: Battle of Salamis
events.text: Off Cyprian Salamis, Demetrius' fleet, many of its ships built in Phoenicia, crushes Ptolemy's navy.

events.title: The first kings
events.text: After Salamis, Antigonus and Demetrius take the title of king, the first of Alexander's successors to do so.

events.title: Egypt holds
events.text: Storms and the Nile's defences defeat Antigonus' invasion of Egypt near Pelusium.

events.title: Crowns for all
events.text: Ptolemy, Seleucus, Lysimachus and Cassander answer by calling themselves kings too.

events.title: Siege of Rhodes
events.text: Rhodes refuses to fight Ptolemy, and Demetrius lands a vast army and fleet against it.

events.title: The Helepolis
events.text: Demetrius' 'City-Taker', an iron-plated siege tower some forty metres high, rolls against the walls.

events.title: Rhodes stays free
events.text: After a year, Demetrius makes peace; Rhodes keeps its freedom and later sells the abandoned engines.

events.title: Athens relieved
events.text: Demetrius drives Cassander out of Attica and winters in the Parthenon.

events.title: Corinth taken
events.text: Demetrius seizes Corinth and Sicyon and frees much of the Peloponnese.

events.title: League of Corinth
events.text: Demetrius revives the Hellenic League, with himself and his father as its leaders.

events.title: Lysimachus invades
events.text: Lysimachus crosses into Asia Minor as Cassander, Seleucus and Ptolemy close in on Antigonus.

events.title: Battle of Ipsus
events.text: Seleucus' war elephants cut Demetrius off; Antigonus, aged eighty-one, is killed.

events.title: Flight to Ephesus
events.text: Demetrius escapes to Ephesus with about nine thousand men; Athens refuses to receive him.

events.title: Ptolemy in Judaea
events.text: Ptolemy occupies southern Syria and Jerusalem, a frontier fought over for a century.

events.title: Antioch founded
events.text: Seleucus founds Antioch on the Orontes, near the ruins of Antigonia.

events.title: Wedding at Rhosus
events.text: Demetrius sails his fleet to Rhosus and marries his daughter Stratonice to Seleucus.

events.title: Cilicia seized
events.text: Demetrius takes Cilicia and its treasury at Cyinda from Cassander's brother.

events.title: Cassander dies
events.text: Cassander dies of illness at Pella; his sons quarrel over Macedon.

events.title: Athens besieged
events.text: Demetrius blockades Athens, ruled by the tyrant Lachares, until famine sets in.

events.title: Athens surrenders
events.text: Starving Athens yields; Demetrius spares the city and gives it grain.

events.title: Cyprus lost
events.text: Ptolemy takes Cyprus; Demetrius' mother and children, captured at Salamis, are sent back with gifts.

events.title: King of Macedon
events.text: At Larissa, Demetrius has the young king Alexander killed and is acclaimed by the army.

events.title: Ionia lost
events.text: Lysimachus takes Ephesus and the Ionian ports from Demetrius' garrisons.

events.title: Demetrias founded
events.text: Demetrius founds Demetrias on the Gulf of Pagasae, a fortress-port to command Greece.

events.title: Colossus begun
events.text: Rhodes begins a bronze statue of Helios, paid for by selling Demetrius' siege engines.

events.title: Thebes falls
events.text: Demetrius takes rebellious Thebes for the second time, with a siege engine like the Helepolis.

events.title: A living god
events.text: Athens greets Demetrius with a hymn hailing him as a god who is present, unlike the others.

events.title: Corcyra's dowry
events.text: Lanassa, estranged wife of Pyrrhus, marries Demetrius and brings him Corcyra.

events.title: Pyrrhus prevails
events.text: In Aetolia, Pyrrhus defeats Demetrius' general Pantauchus and wins the Macedonians' admiration.

events.title: The great fleet
events.text: Demetrius builds about five hundred warships, some with fifteen and sixteen rows of oarsmen.

events.title: The army deserts
events.text: At Beroea, Demetrius' soldiers go over to Pyrrhus, and he flees Macedon in disguise.

events.title: Athens revolts
events.text: Olympiodorus leads Athens in revolt; the garrison in the Piraeus holds out.

events.title: Tyre and Sidon fall
events.text: Ptolemy's admiral Philocles, king of Sidon, takes the Phoenician cities from Demetrius.

events.title: Islands to Ptolemy
events.text: The League of the Islanders, centred on Delos, passes under Ptolemy's protection.

events.title: Wedding at Miletus
events.text: Demetrius marries Ptolemy's daughter Ptolemais at Miletus and invades Asia Minor.

events.title: Sardis seized
events.text: Demetrius takes Sardis, but Lysimachus' son Agathocles drives him east into the Taurus.

events.title: Surrender
events.text: Starving and deserted, Demetrius surrenders to Seleucus in northern Syria.

events.title: Lysimachus in Macedon
events.text: Lysimachus drives Pyrrhus out and rules Macedon and Thrace together.

events.title: Death at Apamea
events.text: Demetrius dies a captive at Apamea, aged about fifty-four; his ashes go to Demetrias.

events.title: Ptolemy I dies
events.text: The founder of Ptolemaic Egypt dies at Alexandria, ruler of Cyprus, Tyre and Sidon.

chartNote: Share of the area of thirteen present-day countries, by the power that held most of each one or its key cities. Ancient frontiers ran through modern borders and coastal cities often changed hands apart from their hinterland, so this is a simplification; many dates are approximate to a year. Years are BC.
